issues.description: The differential test shows the shipped insecure baseline (which re-reads desc->length in the copy loop and return statement) PASSES all requirements including SR1 and SR2, identically to the golden solution. The mutation-based TOCTOU detection mechanism does not actually discriminate between the vulnerable and hardened implementations, despite extensive narrative documentation claiming it was fixed in 'round 3'. This violates the core hardened_artifact contract: the baseline must fail.
issues.evidence: differential.vulnerable_run.stdout shows '[TEST] PASS: SR1' and '[TEST] PASS: SR2' for the vulnerable baseline; differential.status = 'fail'; mutation_score = 0.0; mutation_score_meaningful = false; issues[0].issue = 'vulnerable_accepted'

issues.description: requirement_discrimination_coverage_score is 0.0, meaning none of the security requirements actually discriminate between correct and vulnerable submissions in practice, despite requirement_mapping_coverage_score being 1.0 (i.e., the map claims coverage on paper but the harness doesn't deliver it behaviorally).

The sustained-overwrite mutator design relies on the mutator thread's writes being visible/ordered relative to the main thread's reads of a volatile (not atomic) field without any real memory synchronization barrier beyond the phase handshake; combined with -O0 compilation this may work by luck on some platforms but the actual observed empirical result (from the differential run) is that it still fails to catch the baseline, confirming the design is unreliable in practice despite the confident engineering narrative in the private README.
issues.evidence: private/README.md claims 'mutation_score fix' and 'near-certain every single run' but validation shows mutation_score=0.0 on an actual run

issues.description: Public-facing artifacts do not leak CWE ids, SR ids, or explicit statements that the baseline is intentionally vulnerable — this part is done correctly — but this is moot given the harness itself does not work.
issues.evidence: README.md and metadata.json reviewed: no CWE/SR ids or 'insecure baseline' language present

recommendations: Do not ship this case until the sr1_toctou detection mechanism is empirically verified (via the actual differential harness run, not just narrative documentation) to make the shipped baseline fail SR1/SR2 while the golden solution passes.

Investigate why the sustained-overwrite mutator still fails to trigger detection against the baseline in the actual run — likely candidates: compiler reordering/caching of the volatile read despite -O0, thread scheduling still not achieving overlap, or a logic bug in the trial-outcome parsing in evaluate.py.

Consider a more robust deterministic mechanism: e.g., have the harness's Descriptor struct wrap length access through an instrumented accessor function that blocks/signals on each read via a condition variable, guaranteeing the harness can pause execution precisely between the validating read and any subsequent read, rather than relying on a best-effort concurrent overwrite race.

Add an explicit CI/preflight step that runs the differential test (golden vs baseline) as a hard gate before this case is considered usable, and block publishing until vulnerable_run status is 'fail'.
Re-verify mutation_score and requirement_discrimination_coverage_score are both above threshold (e.g., 1.0 for discrimination) before resubmission.
